text:
Shane Pinto scored twice, the second 2:08 into overtime, to send the Senators past the Avalanche 4-3 after they trailed in the third period. Pinto was drafted 32nd overall in 2019 out of the Tri-City Storm, and he finished the night with two goals and an assist. Drake Batherson tied it with just under four minutes left in regulation, a backhander off assists from Jordan Spence and Pinto.

The Senators got there by taking the early lead and then surviving a game that tilted toward Colorado. OTT scored twice in the first period, Pinto at 7:11 and Tim Stützle at 13:13, but COL out-attempted them 64 to 52 and had the better chances overall. Our numbers on expected goals, which measure the quality of chances taken, put it at 2.93 for COL and 2.55 for OTT. By deserved to win, the share of simulated replays of every shot that a team wins, COL held 57 percent. Special teams made the difference in the middle of the game: the Avalanche scored on 2 of 5 power plays while Ottawa went 0 for 5. Parker Kelly's shorthanded goal in the third came on a chance worth only 3 percent, which tied the game at 2.

Colorado walks away with a point after the better night of chasing play, and with Scott Wedgewood allowing 1.4 more goals than the shots he faced should have produced, according to our numbers. Ottawa takes the extra point and a win built on Pinto's two goals, with Batherson's late tying goal the other big one. The facts we have don't include standings or streaks for either team, so we'll leave it at the result.
